thread:
Maria: ops-bot just fired a spike alert — Sentry events dropped 90% starting at 09:41 UTC. Seeing lots of 429/503 from our observability vendor in the ingestion path. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: Alert: sentry.ingest.error_rate > 75% for 5m. Check: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingest/sentry - dashboard pinned.
Alex: looking. can anyone confirm if this is only exceptions or spans/transactions as well?
Samir: both. transactions appear delayed, exceptions are largely missing. Error count in UI down ~92% vs baseline.
Jen: paging oncall now. @oncall-night you good to take?
incident-bot: Paging on-call: @oncall-night (severity:page). Incident created: INC-2026-0412-01.
oncall-night: on it. joining call in 2. grabbing initial logs.
Maria: quick checks i ran:
```
curl -sS https://sentry-ingest.redwood/api/health | jq .
{"status":"degraded","errors":{"ingest_backend":"rate_limited","upstream":"observability-vendor"}}
```
Alex: vendor status shows a throttling incident: https://status.otherobs.com/incident/9876 - they say token validation service is returning intermittent 401s leading to cascading rate-limits.
Samir: that matches our logs: backend returns a lot of 401/429 during 09:40-09:58. sample from our edge: "error":"upstream 429 - token verification backoff".
Jen: customer impact assessment: Affected: error reporting and crash alerts. Not affecting API requests or generation paths, but customers using Sentry for production alerts will miss signals. mobily support tickets will start coming.
Support Team: prepping customer note draft. Template: "We're investigating an issue with error delivery; raw SDK captures will continue client-side but server-side aggregation may be delayed."
Alex: mitigation options: 1) flip to local fallback pipeline to write events to internal blob store for re-ingest later, 2) temporarily drop sampling to prioritize critical errors, 3) throttle non-critical telemetry at SDK edge. which do we want now?
Samir: start with 2 & 3 — reduce non-actionable noise so vendor can breathe. also enable blob fallback as a near-term buffer (1).
Maria: creating playbook runbook task list in the incident doc.
```
- action: set SENTRY_SAMPLING_RULE to only capture level>=error and explicit allowlists
- action: enable INTERNAL_EVENT_BUFFER=true (writes to s3://redwood-sentry-fallback)
- action: update SDK client sample rate via config push
- action: open vendor support ticket (escalate to P1)
```
oncall-night: pushed sampling change (rollout id 3f2a). verifying throughput.
Alex: on vendor side they've acknowledged and are routing to auth team. their status says partial mitigation at 10:15 UTC.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollout 3f2a -> sampling-change applied to 6 services.
Samir: enabling fallback buffer now. endpoint accepts events but returns 202 locally and stores on S3 for reprocessing.
Jen: setting up a short customer advisory: "We're actively mitigating a third-party ingest disruption causing delayed error signals. We'll update within 2 hours or when reprocessing begins." sending to #support-notices now.
Support Team: posted internal CS template and escalation instructions. recommend proactively emailing 3 enterprise customers who monitor Sentry dashboards.
Maria: vendor sent initial root-cause: upstream auth provider token signer experienced a cache outage leading to high verification latency -> their ingest tier began rejecting until backoff. ETA unknown.
Alex: timeline so far:
- 09:41 UTC: alert fired (ingest error spike)
- 09:44 UTC: on-call paged, initial triage
- 09:52 UTC: vendor status indicates throttling due to token auth failures
- 10:03 UTC: sampling reduced, non-critical telemetry paused
- 10:10 UTC: fallback buffer enabled (s3)
- 10:15 UTC: vendor reports partial mitigation
- 12:30 UTC: we started re-ingestion of buffered events (batch job id reingest-177)
- 13:10 UTC: counts trending back to baseline, but missing alerts require manual re-eval
Samir: re-ingest job notes: we're rate-limiting replays to vendor at 5r/s to avoid re-triggering their limits. job status: running, 1.2M events queued.
oncall-night: handoff to evening oncall (Alex) at 18:00 UTC. leaving summary + playbook: all immediate mitigations applied; monitoring for replay errors.
Alex: acknowledging handoff. docs updated in incident. assigning follow-ups: vendor escalation, post-mortem owner (Maria), customer outreach owner (Support Team), reingest validation (Samir).
Maria: postmortem checklist: root cause, detection timeline, mitigations, follow-ups: add circuit breaker to stop live replays if vendor 429s exceed threshold, add fallback buffer tests in chaos runs, add alert for upstream auth token errors specifically.
Support Team: drafting public status update now. will sync with legal for wording re customer SLAs.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0412-01 moved to 'monitoring' at 13:18 UTC.
Jen: small note — we observed some alerts that should have fired didn't because alert rules were indexed as "events per minute" which was based on processed events. will recommend adding a parallel metric from the edge to detect ingestion losses sooner.
Alex: agreed. open follow-up ticket to add 'edge_ingest_drop_rate' metric and alerting.
Samir: vendor finally confirmed auth provider rotated keys prematurely, causing validation fails. they're rolling an emergency fix. we'll include vendor timeline in the postmortem.
Maria: thanks all. storing incident artifacts: logs, replay job output, vendor ticket link: https://support.otherobs.com/tickets/4567. prepping postmortem draft for tomorrow.
Support Team: customer notifications sent to impacted accounts at 14:00 UTC.
Alex: incident resolved for most customers by 15:05 UTC. closing tasks and scheduling postmortem at 16:00 UTC tomorrow.
oncall-night: handing off to Alex. leaving Slack thread pinned to #incidents. :white_check_mark:
